candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize NCSBN-supported preparation of preceptors in transition-to-practice programs.

options.A: Use a preceptor who has been educated for the preceptor role
options.B: Assign any available nurse without role preparation
options.C: Avoid preceptorship because it delays independent practice
options.D: Use only self-study modules and eliminate direct preceptor feedback

candidate.rationale: NCSBN's national Transition to Practice study found significantly better outcomes when transition programs included a preceptorship and the preceptor was educated for that role. Availability or years of practice alone do not substitute for preparation to function effectively as a preceptor.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Supports use of a preceptorship with a preceptor educated for the role.
candidate.source_locator: Phase I: program characteristic — a preceptorship, and the preceptor should be educated for the role
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
candidate.stem: A nurse educator is selecting a preceptor for a newly licensed nurse entering a transition-to-practice program. Which preparation is specifically supported by NCSBN study findings?

warning: Technical candidate selection only. This file is not clinical audit evidence and does not establish PASS or FAIL.
